Inspiring Young Minds, Ages Three to Thirteen
St John’s Beaumont School is a co-educational preparatory school for boys and girls aged three to thirteen, offering a distinctive blend of tradition and innovation. Set within 70 acres on the edge of Windsor Great Park, our independent school provides an inspiring environment where curiosity, confidence, and character flourish. From our Nursery and Early Years through to Year 8, pupils benefit from small class sizes, specialist teaching, and outstanding facilities including forest trails, an indoor swimming pool, climbing wall, and floodlit courts.
As a private school with over 135 years of excellence, we are proud to prepare children for leading senior schools such as Eton, Harrow, Wellington, and Winchester. Our approach combines strong academic foundations with High Performance Learning, ensuring every child develops the resilience, compassion, and leadership skills needed for life beyond the classroom. With both day and boarding options, St John’s Beaumont offers a caring, inclusive community where every child feels supported to achieve their full potential.
Visit St John’s Beaumont Preparatory School today—where we secure your child’s future.
Confident
All students passed with solid Distinctions in their recent LAMDA exams (December 2024).
Compassionate
All students engage in a full ‘Day of Service’ each year to support local and global charities, as well as visiting residents in local care home facilities.
Resilient
In 2024, all students went to their first or second choice school, with approx. 50% attending Hampton, Harrow, Wellington, Eton, St Paul’s or Winchester.
Headmaster’s welcome
Welcome to St John’s Beaumont Preparatory School, an outstanding preparatory school for boys and girls aged 3 to 13.
Founded in 1888, ours is a school with a remarkable history, a proud Jesuit heritage and, I believe, a tremendously exciting future. At its heart, however, St John’s Beaumont is about something much simpler: children.
I have long been fond of the quote: ‘How can you say, ‘the sky’s the limit’, when there are footsteps on the moon?’
For me, it captures something fundamental about education. We want our children to be happy, curious and ambitious; to have faith in themselves, to discover what they are capable of and, importantly, to enjoy the precious years of childhood along the way.
St John’s Beaumont is also a family. It is the relationships between children and teachers, the friendships between pupils, the partnership with parents and that important sense of belonging which make our school so special.
To discover more about our co-educational journey, high performance learning, and school admissions, we warmly invite you to book a visit to experience our special community and what makes St John’s different.
I very much look forward to welcoming you and your family.
Mr Andrew De Silva Head Master

Elite Football Coaching – A Premier League Partnership With Brentford FC
Enquire About Our Elite Football Coaching Programme
St John’s Beaumont is delighted to launch an exciting new partnership with Brentford Football Club that will bring elite football coaching to pupils across the school.
This collaboration will see specialist coaches from Brentford FC Community Sports Club working with boys and girls of all ages, delivering high-quality football training as part of the curriculum, alongside a broader programme of activities.
This partnership represents a significant step forward in our investments in strengthening the school’s sporting offer. By working closely with experienced coaches, our students will have the chance to develop their skills, build confidence, and deepen their enjoyment of physical activity in an exciting and inspiring environment.
Beyond the school day, there will be further opportunities for pupils to get involved through holiday camps, tournaments, and community events. These initiatives will not only support individual development but also foster teamwork, resilience, and a lifelong love of sport.
This is a genuinely exciting opportunity for the entire St John’s Beaumont community. The school is proud to be working with a Premier League football club, and looks forward to seeing our boys and girls grow, thrive, and achieve through this dynamic new partnership with Brentford Football Club.
“We are delighted to be partnering with St John’s Beaumont School. The Trust has been expanding its delivery outreach into Berkshire and surrounding areas and this presents us with a great opportunity to provide high quality coaching to the students at SJB.”
“We will be working closely with SJB to not only enrich the schools’ sport and activity offer, but also use SJB as a hub to support the wider community through holiday camp provision, school tournaments and other community based events.” – Aaron Davis-Hussain, Community Development Manager for Surrey, Spelthorne and Berkshire at Brentford FCCST.
“We are thrilled to be working with Brentford FC. As a well-established Premier League club, our pupils will benefit from outstanding coaching, and this will open up a further pathway for our talented boys and girls. We are also excited that the partnership will include mentoring for our Sports Scholars, covering areas such as leadership, sports psychology, nutrition, teamwork, tactical awareness and more. Whole-school assemblies featuring representatives from Brentford’s men’s and women’s teams will further inspire our pupils, and with our values so closely aligned, this partnership promises to be extremely impactful.” – Mr Philip Barr, Headmaster of St John’s Beaumont.
“Being able to work alongside Brentford FC allows our coaching to go from strength to strength and reinforces our commitment to provide our pupils with the opportunity to do something greater. I am especially looking forward to building a development pathway for our pupils that really gives them a sense of what high performance training looks and feels like.” – Daniel Manning, Director of Sport.

Creative & Performing Arts
When you believe in developing the whole child, nurturing their imagination, creativity and spirit are hugely important. Creative and performing arts subjects allow children to develop all sides of their character.
The creative arts at St John’s Beaumont School are integrated throughout our curriculum and co-curricular activity programme from Pre-Prep onwards.
The majority of our students learn a musical instrument and this, together with their love of art and drama, makes for a vibrant culture of creativity.
Your child’s progress will be celebrated in our many assemblies, concerts, plays and exhibitions.
Music plays a very important part in the daily life at St John’s Beaumont.
Students receive weekly class music lessons covering listening, performing and composing. All pupils will have the opportunity to try an instrument – in Years 2 and 3, students learn the violin, recorder, and keyboard, progressing to more advanced topics as they move up through the school.
In addition to their timetabled lesson, pupils can join the Pre-Prep choir, the Jubilate Choir or audition to the Chapel Choir. Many pupils also undertake private music tuition on their chosen instrument and have the opportunity to perform either individually or in ensembles in termly music concerts or in the orchestra.
The Music department aims to inspire a love for music but is also committed to developing musical talent in the school. Pupils interested in pursuing a music scholarship at senior school will be well supported to do so through our Music Scholarship programme and Composition Club.
Drama is taught as part of the school curriculum to all children from Nursery up to Year 8. LAMDA examination classes are also available. At St John’s we regard Drama as an important part of the children’s experience at school – it provides an opportunity for creative expression and the discovery of skills that they did not know they had.

All pupils will be involved in school performances during their time at St John’s; the Nativity in Pre-Prep, Middle School Musical and an Upper School performance.

High Performance Learning
At the beginning of 2023, St John’s embarked on a two year journey towards becoming a High Performing School.
The first step on this journey is embracing the mindset that all pupils can become high performers.
We welcomed Professor Deborah Eyre to school for the launch of HPL to our current parents in January 2023. Professor Eyre is the founder of HPL and it is on her meta-analysis of so many educational studies that the programme is based.
What is HPL?
HPL, or High Performance Learning, is a framework of teaching based on research into the way children learn. It reflects what is known about advanced thinking skills and learning behaviours to help all our children develop ‘better brains’.
Research in neuroscience has shown many common characteristics of top performers across a variety of disciplines. These can be grouped into learner “thinking” and learner “behaviour”.
These skills can be taught to all pupils: the evidence is clear that there is not a fixed level of ability amongst young learners, and that the brain is much more malleable than was once thought.
How do we do this at St John’s?
Much of what we already do at St John’s focuses on developing these learning characteristics. With the help of HPL this will become a more structured, whole school, approach.
HPL places emphasis on metacognition: getting children to think about how they think, and what strategies to use in different situations. It also asks them to reflect on the progress they have made and to take responsibility for their future development.
We promote the ‘growth mindset’ philosophy, which is a core part of HPL, and which teaches pupils that making mistakes is a constructive part of learning and something that we continue to encounter throughout life.
It tells those who are not yet performing at a high level (not yet) that their success is down to the focused effort they devote to any task, with good teachers to guide them. It also has a challenging message for those currently doing well but who have a fixed mindset – coasting to success is not an option.
All teaching staff at St John’s are involved in a two-year professional development programme that will see the school become a High Performance School by the end of 2024, with aspirations towards securing World Class status in 2025.
Every child can aspire to success through a St John’s education.
For more information go to the High Performance Learning (HPL website), or alternatively, read Professor Eyre’s book Great Minds and How to Grow Them (also available as an audio book).

pageCache.pageTitle: Wishing Mr Williams A Happy Retirement | St John's Beaumont
pageCache.text:
Wishing Mr Williams A Happy Retirement
At the end of the summer term, we are celebrating the extraordinary career of Geoff Williams, a pillar of the school community and teaching staff since the turn of the millennium. He is retiring and leaving his role as Deputy Head Academic in which he oversees the progress of pupils towards the country’s most prestigious senior schools. However, his time at St John’s has involved outstanding service across all areas of school life that is worth celebrating.
Mr Williams took a leap of faith, moving with his wife, Natalie, and young family from South Africa to the UK twenty-six years ago. As today, it was not uncommon for teachers to join the school from around the world. Geoff brought with him experience of teaching technical drawing and geography in the some of the rainbow nation’s top secondary schools, as well as elite level rugby (Sharks) and water polo coaching experience.
Mr Williams legacy will be his passion for learning through trips and experiences. A stalwart of the school ski trip, he has travelled the world with SJB pupils, from Iceland to the unbelievable experience of boys swimming the Midmar Mile in Cape Town.
On the sports field, Mr William’s rugby teams were always inspired and organised. He played a major roll in years of success the school had along with its formidable reputation on the prep school circuit.
Prep school life has change a great deal in a quarter of a century, yet Geoff’s willingness to put in the extra hours to give pupils fantastic opportunities has never wavered. It is a testament to his resolve and continued pursuit of excellence that St John’s recently received the High Performance Learning World Class School Award. Under his leadership, the evidence presented was among the best ever in the programme.
Throughout his time with us, he has always had the gravitas to engage pupils, bringing a sense of calm and purpose to all his lessons. In the staff room, he will be missed for his dry, self-deprecating sense of humour and unending hardwork. He has been a loyal and dedicated mentor to colleagues, who value his counsel and level-headed approach no matter the circumstances. He departs with lifelong friendships with staff past and present.
As he and his wife move to the coast of the South West of England, more than a generation of St John’s pupils will be sending their thanks and best wishes for his contribution, not only to their education, but sustaining St John’s, time and again.

Our Verse Speaking Final
Last week, pupils from across the school took to the stage for our annual Verse Speaking Final. We were pleased to welcome Mr David Gibbons, Head of English at Eton College, who joined us as this year’s judge and offered thoughtful feedback to our performers.
Throughout the event, pupils presented their chosen pieces with clarity, confidence and evident preparation. Their performances reflected the work they have put into developing their speaking and interpretation skills over the term.
Results
A special mention goes to Andrew W., whose progress has been particularly impressive. When he first joined St John’s, his English-speaking ability was limited, making his success in both the Intermediate and Overall categories a notable achievement.
Thank you to all families, staff and pupils who supported the event. We are proud of every participant for the confidence and enthusiasm they brought to the stage.

Head Master’s Welcome
It is my great pleasure to welcome you to St John’s Beaumont.
Founded in 1888, ours is a school with a remarkable history, a proud Jesuit heritage and, I believe, a tremendously exciting future. At its heart, however, St John’s Beaumont is about something much simpler: children.
I have long been fond of the quote:
‘How can you say, ‘the sky’s the limit’, when there are footsteps on the moon?’
For me, it captures something fundamental about education. We want our children to be happy, curious and ambitious; to have faith in themselves, to discover what they are capable of and, importantly, to enjoy the precious years of childhood along the way. St John’s Beaumont is also a family. It is the relationships between children and teachers, the friendships between pupils, the partnership with parents and that important sense of belonging which make our school so special.
There is, of course, considerably more I could say about what I believe education should be and my hopes and ambitions for the children entrusted to our care.
Better still, come and experience St John’s Beaumont for yourself. I very much look forward to welcoming you and your family.
Founded in 1888, St John’s Beaumont has a remarkable history and a proud tradition of educating children with ambition, purpose and care. Today, that heritage continues to shape a school which places each child at the heart of all that it does.
I have long been fond of the quote: “How can you say, ‘the sky’s the limit’, when there are footsteps on the moon?”
For me, it captures something fundamental about education. Our responsibility should never simply be to prepare children for the next test, the next year group or even the next school. Education should encourage children to look upwards and outwards; to be curious, ambitious and courageous, and to discover possibilities in themselves which they may not yet know exist. That ambition sits particularly comfortably at St John’s Beaumont.
Our Jesuit heritage gives us a distinctive understanding of what education should be. Academic achievement matters enormously, and we want every child to be challenged, inspired and supported to achieve highly. Yet education must be about considerably more than examination results or destination schools. It is about developing the whole person: intellectually, physically, creatively, socially and spiritually. It is about character and faith in oneself.
We want children to leave St John’s as confident but humble young people; curious about the world around them; compassionate towards others; resilient when things do not quite go according to plan; and willing to use their talents for something beyond themselves.
Central to achieving this is happiness. I firmly believe that happy children learn best. Children flourish when they feel known, valued and secure, and when school is somewhere they genuinely want to be. The relationship between school and home is therefore enormously important. Parents entrust us with something extraordinarily precious, and the very best education happens when children, parents and school work together. That sense of family matters: children should know that they belong, parents should feel part of the life of the school, and relationships should extend far beyond the school gates.
Childhood itself is precious too. There should be time to climb trees, play matches, sing, perform, create, explore our extraordinary grounds, make friendships, get muddy, ask difficult questions, laugh, get things wrong and try again. There should be moments of genuine awe and wonder. These experiences are not distractions from a first-class education; they are constituent parts of one.
At the same time, a great preparatory school must prepare children exceptionally well for what comes next. Our pupils move on to some of the country’s leading senior schools, and our responsibility is not simply to help them gain entry, but to ensure that when they arrive, they are ready to flourish there. Independence, confidence, intellectual curiosity and strength of character matter every bit as much as academic preparation.
St John’s Beaumont is fortunate to combine all of this with a tremendous sense of place. Our beautiful buildings and extensive grounds provide an extraordinary environment in which children can learn and grow. Yet buildings and facilities alone do not make a great school. People do. It is the relationships between children and teachers, the friendships between pupils, the partnership with parents and the sense of belonging to the wider St John’s Beaumont family which ultimately give a school its character.
As St John’s Beaumont enters the next chapter of its long history, there is much to celebrate and much to look forward to. We will cherish the traditions and values which have shaped this remarkable school whilst having the confidence to innovate, evolve and ensure that the education we provide remains ambitious, relevant and inspiring for the children growing up in our care today. Of course, no website can truly capture the character of a school. For that, you need to walk through the doors, meet the children and staff, explore the grounds and experience St John’s Beaumont for yourself.
I very much look forward to welcoming you and your family.
Mr Andrew De Silva, Head Master

Jesuit Education
St John’s Beaumont was founded as a Jesuit school, part of a global network of Jesuit educational institutions dedicated to excellence in learning and personal growth. For over 450 years, Jesuit schools and universities have been guided by the principle of improvement in living and learning for the common good (St Ignatius). While St John’s is no longer a Jesuit school, we continue to embrace values that foster intellectual curiosity, resilience, and a commitment to service, ensuring our pupils grow into well-rounded individuals prepared for the future.
JESUIT PUPIL PROFILE
Core Principles
Jesuit education has at its core the principle of cura personalis – care for each person so that they may flourish:
academically
emotionally
socially
physically
spiritually
Teaching and learning
Jesuit schools strive to offer an excellent intellectual formation through outstanding teaching and a Magis curriculum that is as broad and deep, with a rich offering of extra-curricular activities.
Underlying teaching and learning in a Jesuit school is outstanding pastoral care where staff challenge, encouragement and support in the ups and downs of growing up.
RELIGIOUS FORMATION
Religious formation is an important part of the Jesuit education at St John’s, giving pupils the opportunity to encounter God in prayer, reflection and worship, study, and in the service of others.
JESUIT PUPIL PROFILE

School History
St John’s Beaumont was opened in 1888 initially as the preparatory school for the Jesuit public school Beaumont College, which was also situated in Old Windsor. It was designed by John Frances Bentley, one of the most famous architects of his day who later went on to design Westminster Cathedral in London.
It is called St John’s after St John Berchmans, a Dutch saint who died whilst still very young, aged 21, and who was canonized by Pope Leo XIII in the year 1888.
In 1967 the Society of Jesus took the decision to close Beaumont College and move many of the pupils to another Jesuit school in Lancashire (Stonyhurst College). St John’s retained the sports field of Beaumont upon its closure; today known as the ‘Beaumont Flats’.
St John’s is unique in that it was purpose-built for 60 boys aged between 7 and 13 and this can still be seen in the provision of 60 carved wooden chapel pews and 60 individual dormitory cubicles. However over recent years the school has expanded both its classroom provision and its facilities to accommodate over 300 pupils.
More recent additions to the school’s facilities have included a 25 metre indoor swimming pool, a purpose-built sports centre opened by Her Majesty the Queen in 2009, art studio and library, music school, science laboratory and pre-preparatory department & playground. In September 2023, the school officially became co-educational, welcoming girls into Pre-Prep.
